annotationRationale: Shifting the recurrence gives uniform ratio bounds, which compare its terms with geometric sequences. Inequality properties and a short binomial bound locate the threshold index.
sourceMethod: Followed the official substitution and geometric comparison. Reorganized the endpoint estimates as direct checks at indices 80 and 200, avoiding fractional exponents.

review.mathCheck: The substitution gives \(y_{n+1}=y_n(y_n+9)/(y_n+10)\). Positivity and decrease imply \((9/10)^n\le y_n\le(10/11)^n\). Since \((9/10)^4>1/2\) and \((11/10)^{10}>2\), we obtain \(y_{80}>2^{-20}\) and \(y_{200}<2^{-20}\). Thus the least index exists and satisfies \(81\le m\le200\), entirely within choice C.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA AMC 10B solution 24, pages 12 and 13. It preserves the shifted recurrence, geometric bounds and binomial estimate. Checking indices 80 and 200 establishes the same integer bounds as the official argument.
review.annotationCheck: All selected concepts are used, with recurrence handling and geometric comparison assessed and inequality manipulation and binomial expansion supporting them. The explanation distinguishes the nonlinear sequence from its geometric bounds.
